title: Fibrant objects of the symmetric operadic pattern model category are inert-marked symmetric infinity operads
statement: Use symmetric infinity operads, their inert edges, the pattern $\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{sym}}$ on $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ and the model category $\mathsf M=\mathsf M_{\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{sym}}}$ of [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-fibration-recognition], the $\mathfrak P$-fibered marked objects of [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy], and the model structure of [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus]. Let $(Z,T)$, with marking-preserving structure map $q:Z\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$, be a fibrant object of $\mathsf M$. Then $q$ is a symmetric infinity operad in the sense of [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-fibration-recognition]: it is an inner fibration with $q$-cocartesian lifts of all inert pointed maps; for every $n\geq0$ the colour projections induce an equivalence $Z_{\langle n\rangle}\simeq Z_{\langle1\rangle}^n$; and for all vertices $y$ over $\langle m\rangle$ and $z$ over $\langle n\rangle$, every pointed map $\phi:\langle m\rangle\to\langle n\rangle$ and every choice of $q$-cocartesian edges $z\to z_i$ over the colour projections $\rho_i$, composition gives an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}^{\phi}_Z(y,z)\simeq\prod_{i=1}^n\operatorname{Map}^{\rho_i\phi}_Z(y,z_i)$, the superscripts denoting homotopy fibres of the maps of mapping spaces over the indicated pointed maps. Moreover $T$ is exactly the set of inert edges of $Z$, so $(Z,T)=Z^{\mathrm{in}}$. The case $n=0$ is included: $Z_{\langle0\rangle}$ is equivalent to $\Delta^0$ and each $\operatorname{Map}^{\phi}_Z(y,z)$ with $z$ over $\langle0\rangle$ is contractible. Together with the fibrancy of $Q^{\mathrm{in}}$ in [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-fibration-recognition], the fibrant objects of $\mathsf M$ are exactly the objects $Q^{\mathrm{in}}$ for small symmetric infinity operads $Q$.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Proposition 2.1.4.6 and its proof (fibrant objects of the infinity-preoperad model structure are exactly the inert-marked infinity operads), using the pattern fibrancy conditions of Appendix B; not archived in literature/ (WANTED). The pattern unpacking was formerly inlined in step 7 of lem-coef-operadic-approximation-marked-equivalence.

proof.text: Put $C=N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$. By the model-calculus theorem, fibrancy of $(Z,T)$ means that it is $\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{sym}}$-fibered. Conditions (i) and (ii) therefore give the inner fibration $q$, cocartesian lifts of every inert map, and the equality of $T$ with the cocartesian edges over inert maps. Also $Z$ is a quasicategory: the image of an inner horn fills in $C$ (a string of composable arrows in an ordinary category has its composite), and the inner lifting property of $q$ then fills the given horn in $Z$.

source.place: Theorem B.0.20(F), Definition B.0.19(1)-(4), specialized to the fully scaled pattern

proof.text: Let $K_n$ be the discrete simplicial set on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Condition (iii) says that $Z\times_C K_n^{\triangleleft}\to K_n^{\triangleleft}$ is classified by a limiting diagram in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. Straightening identifies its vertex with $Z_{\langle n\rangle}$, its boundary with the $n$ copies of $Z_{\langle1\rangle}$, and its legs with colour-projection transport. A limit of this discrete diagram is its product. These products in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ are the categorical products by the straightening theorem, so the comparison is $Z_{\langle n\rangle}\simeq Z_{\langle1\rangle}^n$. Here the comparison of two product cones is invertible directly from their universal properties: the tuple of projections gives the map in each direction, and both composites are the identity because their projections are the identity tuple. This includes the empty product, whose object is the terminal category $\Delta^0$.

source.place: Definition B.0.19(5); Definition 2.1.1.10(3) and Remark 2.1.1.14; use the project colour-projection pattern directly

proof.text: Fix $z$ over $\langle n\rangle$ and any specified $q$-cocartesian edges $e_i:z\to z_i$ over the colour projections. These edges define a section $s$ of $Z\times_C K_n^{\triangleleft}\to K_n^{\triangleleft}$: the cone has only the $n$ legs as nondegenerate positive-dimensional simplices. Each $e_i$ remains cocartesian in this pullback, since a cocartesian horn lifting problem there is exactly a horn problem for $q$ with its base simplex fixed by the map to the cone. Degenerate edges are cocartesian by the composition-initiality lemma. Thus $s$ is a cocartesian section, and condition (iv) says that its composite in $Z$ is a $q$-limit diagram. This works for every chosen family $e_i$, and for the section consisting just of $z$ when $n=0$.

source.place: Definition B.0.19(6); the project cone has discrete boundary and includes arity zero

proof.text: Fix any $y$ over $\langle m\rangle$ and test the relative-limit property of $s$ against the constant cone $t$ at $y$, with all legs identities. Write $M=\operatorname{Map}_Z(y,z)$ and $V=\prod_i\operatorname{Map}_Z(y,z_i)$; write $M_C=\operatorname{Map}_C(\langle m\rangle,\langle n\rangle)$ and $V_C=\prod_i\operatorname{Map}_C(\langle m\rangle,\langle1\rangle)$. The join-cone mapping formula, natural for boundary restriction and postcomposition by $q$, identifies $\operatorname{Map}(t,s)$ with $V\times^h_V M\simeq M$ and its boundary restriction with $M\to V$, whose components are composition with $e_i$. The first map $V\to V$ is the identity up to the unit homotopy in the mapping-composition lemma, since the legs of $t$ are identities. Evaluation contracts the path-pullback of an identity map to its other factor. The same calculation in $C$ identifies the lower row with $M_C\to V_C$. The relative-limit square of the relative-cone definition therefore says precisely that the natural comparison $M\to V\times^h_{V_C}M_C$ is an equivalence. This computation uses full mapping spaces, including their triangle homotopies.

source.place: Definition B.0.19(6); explicit unpacking through the cited relative-cone and join-cone statements

proof.text: For an ordinary category $I$, its right-pinched mapping space from $a$ to $b$ in $N(I)$ is the discrete simplicial set $\operatorname{Hom}_I(a,b)$. Indeed an $r$-simplex is a functor $[r+1]\to I$ whose first $r+1$ vertices and entire initial face are constant at $a$, and whose last vertex is $b$. Its only remaining datum is the arrow $a\to b$; the initial arrows are identities, so every arrow to the last vertex equals that one. All simplicial operators keep this arrow fixed. Consequently $M_C$ and $V_C$ are discrete, and the lower horizontal map sends $\phi$ to $(\rho_i\phi)_i$.

source.place: Definition 2.1.1.10(2); direct calculation from the nerve and right-pinched mapping-space definitions

proof.text: Regard the comparison in step 4 as a map over $M_C$ and apply homotopy-fiber detection with the identity equivalence of $M_C$. For every $\phi:\langle m\rangle\to\langle n\rangle$ this gives an equivalence from $\operatorname{Map}^{\phi}_Z(y,z)$ to the homotopy fiber over $\phi$ of $V\times^h_{V_C}M_C\to M_C$. Pasting homotopy-pullback squares identifies the latter with the homotopy fiber of $V\to V_C$ over $(\rho_i\phi)_i$. In the path-pullback model this fiber is $\prod_i\operatorname{Map}^{\rho_i\phi}_Z(y,z_i)$: a point, path, or higher simplex in a product is exactly a tuple of the corresponding data, since simplicial products and the interval mapping object are computed coordinatewise. The induced equivalence is composition with the chosen $e_i$, as step 4 identifies its boundary restriction. This proves the required mapping-space product formula for every choice of cocartesian projections.

source.place: Definition 2.1.1.10(2); homotopy-fiber extraction from the relative-limit square

proof.text: When $n=0$, step 2 gives $Z_{\langle0\rangle}\simeq\Delta^0$, so in particular this fiber is nonempty. In step 4 both $V$ and $V_C$ are empty products, hence points; $M_C$ is also a point because there is exactly one pointed map $\langle m\rangle\to\langle0\rangle$. Thus $M\simeq M_C\simeq\Delta^0$, and the homotopy fiber over that unique map is contractible, as asserted. No existence of a colour is needed: if $Z_{\langle1\rangle}$ is empty, step 2 makes the positive-arity fibers empty while retaining the terminal zero fiber.

source.place: Definition 2.1.1.10, including the empty output family; empty-cone conditions in Definition B.0.19(5)-(6)

proof.text: Steps 1, 2 and 6 give exactly the inner-fibration, inert-lifting, fiber-product and mapping-product clauses of the symmetric-operad definition in the recognition node. By step 1 the marking is exactly its inert marking, so $(Z,T)=Z^{\mathrm{in}}$. Conversely the first assertion of the recognition node says that $Q^{\mathrm{in}}$ is fibrant in this very model category for every small symmetric infinity operad $Q$. The two implications establish the asserted classification of fibrant objects.

I read the item's 8 steps against the full statement of every node they cite, and each step holds. Step 1: by model-calculus, fibrant means P-fibered; conditions (i) and (ii) give the inner fibration, the inert cocartesian lifts and T = the inert edges, so (Z,T) = Z^in. Step 2: condition (iii) for the discrete colour cone is a product cone in Cat_inf, and straightening gives the fibers, the transports and terminal = Delta^0, hence Z_<n> ≃ Z_<1>^n, with n=0 included. Step 3: an arbitrary family of cocartesian projections is a cocartesian section; cocartesian edges stay cocartesian after pullback, and composition-initiality says degenerate edges are cocartesian; so (iv) applies. Step 4: testing the relative-limit square on the constant cone at y, the join-cone formula and the unit homotopy reduce it to M ≃ V x^h_{V_C} M_C. It also uses two one-line facts not spelled out: mapping spaces in a product are products, and equivalences preserve mapping spaces. Step 5: mapping spaces in the nerve are discrete; I checked this directly. Step 6: fiber detection over id_{M_C}, then pasting, then coordinatewise path fibers. Step 7: n=0 and the no-colour case are consistent. Step 8: the clauses match the recognition node's definition, and the reverse direction is the recognition node's first assertion. No hypothesis is added, nothing is circular, and no node restates a clause of the item. Every cited statement is in unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, so no tool_uses are needed; def-cbc is only a definition.
